### Issue Description

failed_line() never gets fired.

### Expected Behavior

failed_line() to get fired.

comments:
Up to a certain degree, read_csv seems to absorb unexpected columns as MultiIndex:

```py
from io import StringIO

import pandas as pd

def fun(xs):
    return None

handle = StringIO("a\na,b\nc,d,e\nf,g,h")  # multiindex
print(pd.read_csv(handle, engine="python", on_bad_lines=fun))
#     a.1
# a b
# c d   e
# f g   h

handle = StringIO("a\na,b\nc,d,e\nf,g,h,i")  # calls fun (but also uses multiindex)
print(pd.read_csv(handle, engine="python", on_bad_lines=fun))
#     a.1
# a b
# c d   e
```

Could you provide a minimal and reproducible example?

https://matthewrocklin.com/blog/work/2018/02/28/minimal-bug-reports
@twoertwein You could supress this through index_col=False

[cct15_bad_minimal.csv](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/files/8383818/cct15_bad_minimal.csv)
[pandas_error.py.txt](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/files/8383872/pandas_error.py.txt)

You will have to rename pandas_error.py.txt to pandas_error.py.
Lines 2,3 and 4 represent the broken csv.
Could you create something that we can copy and paste?

> @twoertwein You could supress this through index_col=False

Still seems to infer a multiindex (I updated my above example slightly):

```py
handle = StringIO("a\na,b\nc,d,e\nf,g,h")  # multiindex
print(pd.read_csv(handle, engine="python", on_bad_lines=fun, index_col=False))
#     a.1
# a b
# c d   e
# f g   h
handle = StringIO("a\na,b\nc,d,e\nf,g,h,i")  # calls fun (but also uses multiindex)
print(pd.read_csv(handle, engine="python", on_bad_lines=fun, index_col=False))
#     a.1
# a b
# c d   e
```
Hm this seems off. I think the c engine works as expected, but would have to look closer
